issues.legal_issue: A certified copy of an old statement does not establish a mortgage acknowledgment when the original and proof of the signers’ signatures and identities are absent, and the available presumptions do not supply that proof.
material_facts: The suits sought redemption of mortgages and relied on statements in mutation proceedings as acknowledgments to overcome the limitation bar.
The statements were produced only as certified copies; the originals were not produced and no witness proved that the originals were signed by the mortgagors or their representatives.
The statements were not entries in the record of rights, and no duty was shown requiring the official to take the signatures in the signers’ presence or identify the signers.
issues.conclusion: The certified copies could not serve as acknowledgments, and the claims that depended on them could not succeed as claims brought within time.
issues.legal_principle: Section 90 of the Evidence Act did not permit a presumption as to signatures on an original that was not produced merely because a certified copy was produced; Harihar Prasad Singh v. Mst. of Munshi Nath Prasad was followed. Section 44 of the Punjab Land Revenue Act concerns presumptions about entries in the record of rights and did not apply to the statements at issue. Section 114(e) of the Evidence Act concerns the regular performance of official acts and did not establish the genuineness of a signature or the identity of an executant unless the official had a duty to take the signature in the person’s presence and identify that person.

rule.if: mortgage_redemption_suit and acknowledgment_used_to_avoid_limitation and certified_copy_only and original_not_produced and signer_identity_unproved and not record_of_rights_entry and not official_duty_to_identify_signer

predicates.mortgage_redemption_suit: The claimant brought a suit to redeem a mortgage.
predicates.acknowledgment_used_to_avoid_limitation: The claimant relied on a statement as an acknowledgment to bring the redemption claim within time.
predicates.certified_copy_only: The claimant produced only a certified copy of the statement.
predicates.original_not_produced: The original statement was not produced in court.
predicates.signer_identity_unproved: No evidence established that the original was signed by the mortgagor or the mortgagor’s representative.
predicates.record_of_rights_entry: The statement was an entry in the record of rights.
predicates.official_duty_to_identify_signer: The official had a duty to take the signature in the signer’s presence and identify the signer.

issues.definition: When a redemption claimant relies on an acknowledgment but produces only a copy without proof of the signer’s identity, and neither the record-of-rights nor official-duty facts apply, the copy does not establish the acknowledgment.

issues.legal_issue: The period for bringing a mortgage-redemption suit is not enlarged merely because a statutory summary application was dismissed and the suit was brought within the period for challenging that dismissal.
material_facts: The claimants applied under a statutory summary procedure concerning redemption, and their application was dismissed.

The subsequent redemption suit was brought within one year of the dismissal, but the claim was otherwise barred by the limitation period for a redemption suit, even after excluding the time spent pursuing the application.
issues.conclusion: The time allowed to sue to establish rights after the summary order did not enlarge the limitation period for a redemption suit, and the suit was dismissed as time-barred.
issues.legal_principle: Section 12 of the Redemption of Mortgages (Punjab) Act, 1913 makes an order under sections 6 to 11 conclusive unless a suit to establish rights in respect of the mortgage is brought within the prescribed period. It does not extend the limitation period applicable to a suit for redemption. The court considered prior Lahore High Court decisions on the effect of failing to bring a suit under section 12 but found they did not support an extension of the redemption limitation period.

rule.if: mortgage_redemption_suit and summary_redemption_application_dismissed and ordinary_redemption_limitation_expired and suit_within_period_to_challenge_order

predicates.mortgage_redemption_suit: The claimant brought a suit to redeem a mortgage.
predicates.summary_redemption_application_dismissed: The claimant’s application under a summary redemption procedure was dismissed.
predicates.ordinary_redemption_limitation_expired: The limitation period for bringing the redemption suit had expired.
predicates.suit_within_period_to_challenge_order: The claimant brought the suit within the period allowed to challenge the summary order.

issues.definition: When a redemption suit is otherwise out of time, bringing it within the period for challenging a dismissed summary application does not extend the time for the redemption suit.
